data.title: Vault Of Whispers
data.statement:
The Vault of Whispers

 Goal

A dead-drop server exposes `N` intercepted binary key-fragments. Intelligence says the final unlock code is produced by **XOR-ing together some subset** of these fragments — but agents can only carry a handful of fragments on an extraction run, so you must find the **smallest possible subset** that reconstructs the code exactly.

### Rules

You are given `N` non-negative integers (the key fragments) and one target integer `T` (the unlock code).

You must choose a subset of the fragments (each used at most once, order doesn't matter) whose XOR equals exactly `T`. The empty subset is valid and XORs to `0`.

Output the size of the **smallest such subset**, or `-1` if no subset reaches `T`.

`N` is deliberately large enough that trying every one of the `2^N` subsets will not finish in time. You will need an approach that avoids full enumeration.

### Example

With fragments `5 3 9 12 6` and target `10`:

`3 XOR 9 = 10`, and no single fragment equals `10`, so the minimum subset size is `2`.
